honing_confound: Shield efficiency and tier standing are honing-indexed. Shield values (60% HP equivalents from Battleready effects) scale with gear honing. Party damage buff value is not strongly confounded but tier placement reflects T4 meta.

delivery.evidence: Primary skills are melee attacks with a lance+gun-shield combination. Shield Bash, Charged Stinger, Surge Cannon (short-range cannonball), Bash, Gunlance Wave. Most delivery is melee or very short-range projectile (Surge Cannon fires ~3m forward).

footprint.evidence: Most skills land in small directional cones or point-blank radii. Shield-based skills are self-centered AoE. Surge Cannon is a short-range line AoE. No wide-zone coverage.

geo_text: Tanky melee kit. Combat Readiness Gunlancer fights at point-blank range with shield bashes and Gunlance attacks. Skills hit in small frontal arcs. Defensive Stance (Z) is self-centered and redirects incoming damage. Party Battlefield Shield radiates from caster position to nearby allies. All damage output is melee/short-range.

control.evidence: No primary CC ailments in identity. Shield Bash can stagger bosses. Combat Readiness is the support-adjacent warrior archetype — does not rely on CC. Primary identity effect is defensive/protective.

defense.evidence: Combat Readiness identity: Defensive Stance deflects incoming damage. Battlefield Shield places party shield. Class has highest tankiness in game — shield absorption + heavy armor stats. Identity doubles down on shields and damage mitigation rather than dodge. Push immunity inherent.

economy.builder_source: Blue (normal) skills generate Combat Power/Identity Gauge. Defensive Stance consumption is moderate. Battlefield Shield consumes full gauge.
economy.plain_text: Identity gauge fills via blue skills. TWO uses: (1) Defensive Stance (Z) = tanking mode with incoming damage deflection; active while gauge deplets; (2) Battlefield Shield = party shield (full-gauge consume, one-shot use). Combat Readiness identity emphasizes Defensive Stance over Battlefield Shield, maximizing tanking uptime. Dual-spend structure makes this the richest identity economy in the Warrior archetype.

element.evidence: Gunlancer skills deal Physical damage. Surge Cannon may have a separate damage type — not confirmed from live sources.

movement.evidence: Very low mobility. Gunlancer is the slowest Warrior. Defensive Stance restricts movement (stationary or near-stationary). 'Lack of mobility' noted across multiple guides. No dash equivalent in primary rotation.

attr.evidence: Melee/point-blank range. Shield-centric engagement style requires standing in melee range.

range.evidence: All skills land within melee engagement distance. Surge Cannon extends to ~5m but is still very short-range.

tempo.evidence: Combat Readiness is a sustained identity: Defensive Stance toggles on/off to manage damage intake. No burst window structure. Consistent DPS with permanent defensive uptime.

amp.value: Party +10% damage dealt (Battlefield Shield buff); self Defensive Stance deflection
amp.evidence: Combat Readiness identity provides party damage amplification (from Shield buff) + self damage mitigation. Damage dealt by Combat Readiness Gunlancer is moderate — not the identity's primary amplification focus.

proxy.evidence: No summons or remote effects. All output is direct melee.

commitment.evidence: Key skills (Charged Stinger, Gunlance Wave) have charge animations. Defensive Stance is an instant toggle.

mechanics_notes: 1) Combat Readiness is Lost Ark's premier 'support-tank' hybrid — damage is below average but the class provides genuine party protection (Battlefield Shield) on top of personal tankiness. Closest genre analog: D3 zBarb in role function (protect party, aggregate enemies) though execution is entirely different. 2) Taunt mechanic via Endure Pain forces boss aggro — no engine equivalent. 3) The blue/red skill distinction (blue = normal skills that generate gauge; red = specialized Gunlance attacks) is a dual-skill-track that Combat Readiness leans away from (uses mostly blue). This is a meaningful design pattern — the identity gates which half of the skill set is primary. 4) Party shield as identity spend is one of the strongest examples in the genre of an identity skill whose primary beneficiary is allies, not the caster.
stabilization_patch: Combat Readiness was the dominant Gunlancer identity through 2022-2024 in raid contexts. Support-tank demand drove consistent tier placement.
tier_standing_release: S-tier (top support-tank at global launch; highest stagger output + party utility)
tier_standing_current: A-tier (Maxroll 2025 community tier list; Paladin and Bard compete for support slot, limiting Gunlancer adoption, but Combat Readiness remains valued in specific raid compositions). HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: tier placement reflects T4 meta where shield values scale with gear honing.

honing_confound: Crit damage amplification through red skills scales with honing tier. Tier standing reflects T4 meta where Lone Knight is primarily a solo/chaos-dungeon identity rather than raid meta.

delivery.evidence: Red Gunlance skills are the primary damage tools. Gunlance skills have more ranged/explosive delivery than blue skills — includes short-range cannonball/shell attacks alongside melee lance strikes.

footprint.evidence: Red skills like Leap Attack, Counter Gunlance, and Gunlance Shot create small AoE at impact points. Still fundamentally melee/short-range.

geo_text: DPS-focused Gunlancer using red Gunlance skills (shell attacks, explosive rounds, lance charges) rather than shield utility. More aggressive positioning required than Combat Readiness — glass cannon by Gunlancer standards. Defensive Stance is the only identity use (Battlefield Shield removed), and it drains 2× as fast.

control.evidence: Lone Knight's red skill damage focus reduces defensive/CC utility further. Stagger on key attacks remains but not the identity's purpose.

defense.evidence: Lone Knight removes Battlefield Shield (party defensive tool). Defensive Stance (only remaining identity use) still provides self-defense but drains fast. Significantly less defensive profile than Combat Readiness — closer to a standard DPS warrior.

economy.builder_source: Red skills generate some gauge; blue skills still generate it. But only Defensive Stance uses it (Battlefield Shield removed).
economy.plain_text: Same gauge generation as Combat Readiness but only one spend option: Defensive Stance. Drains at 2× rate, meaning toggles are shorter, requiring more active management. Simplifies the dual-economy of Combat Readiness to a single-spend meter.

element.evidence: Red Gunlance skills deal Physical damage. Explosive shells may have separate physics but likely still Physical attribute.

movement.evidence: Still low mobility but slightly better than Combat Readiness due to more aggressive skill set (Counter Gunlance has a dash component). Still categorized as 'poor mobility' class overall.

attr.evidence: Still primarily melee with slightly longer effective range from shell attacks.

range.evidence: Red skills extend range slightly vs blue skills. Counter Gunlance has a forward dash. Shell attacks land at ~5-8m.

tempo.evidence: Lone Knight emphasizes high-damage red skill bursts rather than sustained tanking uptime. More burst-focused than Combat Readiness's sustained identity.

amp.value: Crit Rate and Crit Damage significantly buffed on red skills; Defensive Stance reduced uptime
amp.evidence: Lone Knight engraving 'heavily buffs the critical chance and damage of Gunlance skills.' This is the core amplification trade vs Combat Readiness's party protection.

commitment.evidence: Red skills have charge animations similar to blue skills but with higher damage payoff.

mechanics_notes: 1) Lone Knight is the 'selfish DPS' Gunlancer — trades party utility (Battlefield Shield) for personal damage. Represents a meaningful design choice in LA where a fundamentally 'support tank' class can opt into a pure-damage identity at significant cost to party contribution. 2) Stagger + Part Break contribution is higher in Lone Knight via red skills (higher ratings on explosive attacks). Destruction on lance charges. These are boss mechanic mechanics (no engine equivalent). 3) Lone Knight is less popular in raid content because parties expect Gunlancers to provide Battlefield Shield — removing it requires a party composition adjustment.
stabilization_patch: Lone Knight was used in chaos dungeon clearing and solo content from launch. Never dominated raid meta.
tier_standing_release: B-tier at launch (niche vs Combat Readiness)
tier_standing_current: C-tier in endgame raids; B-tier in solo content. HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: tier reflects party-composition meta bias toward Battlefield Shield; pure damage output is competitive but opportunity cost is high.
